title: Errors and debugging

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
A debugger reveals values and execution steps; inspect the failed assumption instead of patching by guesswork.
CORE EXPLANATION
A traceback shows the exception type and the line where it surfaced in the call chain. Read the final exception, reduce the input to a small case, and step through it in a debugger.
EXAMPLE CODE
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.
EXPECTED RESULT

LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`value = int('42')` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`assert value == 42` — Checks a developer assumption early; relying on assert alone does not protect user input.
`print(value)` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Record the inputs and conditions that produce a failure instead of hiding it.

spans.title: Watch out
spans.text: Never log passwords, tokens, or personal data; a type hint is not runtime validation.
COMMON MISTAKES
Keep tests deterministic and make log levels and type contracts explicit.
